A 29-year-old woman visits her primary care physician due to non-bloody nipple discharge that has
been occurring for the past month and occasionally stains her clothing. She consumes 2 to 3 alcoholic
drinks daily and smokes one pack of cigarettes per day. She is undergoing outpatient psychiatric
treatment following a recent hospitalization for auditory hallucinations and is on an unspecified
medication prescribed by her psychiatrist. She also reports frequent headaches. Her vital signs include
a temperature of 98.6°F (37.0°C), blood pressure of 152/75 mmHg, pulse of 69/min, respirations of
12/min, and oxygen saturation of 98% on room air. Physical examination reveals bilateral galactorrhea
upon palpation. A urine pregnancy test is negative. What is the most appropriate next step in
management? Answer Choices: (A) CT scan of the head (B) TSH level (C) MRI of the pituitary gland
(D) Serum estrogen level (E) Discontinuation of current psychiatric medications (F) Referral to
endocrinology (G) Observation and follow-up in 3 months (H) Mammography (I) Serum prolactin level
(J) Dopamine agonist therapy
 A. CT scan of the head
B. Referral to endocrinology
